description: The figure is a pie chart representing the distribution of sources/outlets referenced in the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing 17 slices (categories) labeled around the circle with numeric values printed inside each wedge. The largest slices are Breitbart (blue, 14) and Other (gray, 13), followed by Drudge Report (orange, 8) and The Daily Caller (green, 8), then The Huffington Post (red, 7), NPR (purple, 6), Vox (brown, 6), The Guardian (pink, 5), BBC (gray, 5), RT (yellow-green, 4), and seven smaller slices each labeled 3: Daily Kos (light blue), National Review (teal), Daily Mail (orange), Redstate (green), Fox News (red), CNN (purple), and Shareblue/PoliticusUSA (brown). There is no separate legend; labels are placed outside the pie with leaderless positioning, and the slice values are shown inside the wedges. No slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the slices are not strictly ordered by size around the chart.
